pr_title: glTF: Fix loading external images as buffer
pr_body:
We should first attempt loading as external files, thus creating a dependency.
Loading as a buffer should only be used as fallback to support manually loading
as PNG or JPEG depending on the defined mimeType.

Fixes #44309, was a regression from #42504.
pr_comments: Thank you for catching the regression :)

I tweaked some files and mime types to create bugs and see how this code handles it, it seems fine.
```
-rw-r--r-- 1 akien akien 312910 Jan  5 16:05 rock03.badext
-rw-r--r-- 1 akien akien      0 Jan  5 16:34 TexturesCom_WoodPlanksClean0061_1_seamless_S.badextandtruncated
```
```
    "images" : [
        {
            "mimeType" : "image/jpeg",
            "name" : "TexturesCom_WoodPlanksClean0061_1_seamless_S",
            "uri" : "textures/TexturesCom_WoodPlanksClean0061_1_seamless_S.badextandtruncated"
        },
        {
            "mimeType" : "badmime/type",
            "name" : "rock03",
            "uri" : "textures/rock03.badext"
        }
    ],
```
```
ERROR: No loader found for resource: res://import/textures/TexturesCom_WoodPlanksClean0061_1_seamless_S.badextandtruncated.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:206)
WARNING: glTF: Image index '0' with MIME type 'image/jpeg' couldn't be loaded as a buffer from URI: res://import/textures/TexturesCom_WoodPlanksClean0061_1_seamless_S.badextandtruncated. Skipping it.
     at: _parse_images (modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp:2936)
ERROR: No loader found for resource: res://import/textures/rock03.badext.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:206)
WARNING: glTF: Image index '1' with MIME type 'badmime/type' couldn't be loaded from URI: res://import/textures/rock03.badext. Skipping it.
     at: _parse_images (modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp:2943)
```
The glTF can be loaded, the materials don't have textures since both failed loading and were skipped.

Note that it's not completely failproof, as if e.g. you pass a valid MIME type but an invalid type of file, the load as buffer will fail with an `ERR_FAIL_COND_V`, so it will abort importing the glTF.

Could possibly be improved further but IMO that's already a good amount of failure that we handle gracefully, more than that should likely be handled by fixing the broken glTF images. In any case that's outside the scope of this PR.

> Edited: the blender gltf2 goes as far to make placeholders instead of null.

We could do that, but that code should likely be reworked for it. I'm not sure how important it is though, if some external textures are missing, Godot will report them as such already (with a noisy error, which is less elegant than the Blender solution, but better than nothing).

issue_context.title: Godot 3.2.4 does not actually use separate textures for GLTF files exported with separate textures enabled (they're instead embedded in the materials).
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues for potential duplicates before filing yours:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues?q=is%3Aissue
-->

**Godot version:** v3.2.4.beta4.official, affects master as well.
<!-- Specify commit hash if using non-official build. -->

**OS/device including version:** Linux Mint 20 x86_64

**Issue description:**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/781121/101961496-21d6d900-3c0a-11eb-82f6-997b0de2be81.png)
When exporting a blender scene to GLTF for use in Godot 3.2.4.beta4, with the export settings shown in the screenshot above, with textures exported into a folder instead of packed into the GLTF itself, Godot is supposed to use those textures in the resulting SpatialMaterial resources after importing.

beta4 currently fails to do this, even with separate textures enabled, it always ends up packing the textures directly into the SpatialMaterial, leaving the textures in the exported folder unused.

This does not happen in 3.2.3, so I'm guessing some regression may have happened at some point.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Setup a blender scene in a recent version of blender, 2.8 or 2.9.
2. Make sure textures are used in it. (ofcourse)
3. When exporting to GLTF, make sure to set it so it exports textures separately. (as shown above)
4. After exporting to Godot, right click the resulting SpatialMaterial(s), and click "Edit Dependencies".
5. Notice that there are no dependencies.
comments: I hope this one can get fixed before 3.2.4.stable releases, my workflow relies heavily on this working correctly, since GLTF currently works the best out of all the export options available right now for me.

Are you able to do a bisect to find the commit that change the behaviour? I have some suspects.

Like use git bisect and take your project and do a check on the bug until you find a version that doesn't error. Then tell me the version that errors and the version that doesn't error.

@fire
For what its worth, all of the 3.2.4 betas suffer from this issue, so it has to be a commit from sometime before beta 1.
I found 3 commits that involve GLTF related changes for beta1, I have no way of knowing if any of them are related to this problem though.

460ab35
177d16c
9529ce4

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/9529ce41eb4c58a395962ea3cdd61f090717fd54#diff-391b8dac176705a7434fd9ca93ac540183658308fcb6a91cc40f6f2ecd4439baR1384 is suspicious, but I'm currently busy and in the middle of something.
On an extra note, this issue affects the 4.0 master branch as well currently, but I'm guessing this will probably be resolved with the upcoming 3D asset import rework for 4.0.
Might indeed be related to #42504, I'll have a look. It would help me out if there was a minimal reproduction project that I can use right away to debug the issue.

Thanks! I exported as described with Blender 2.91.0, and it seems to work fine for me in Godot 3.2.4 beta 4 and latest `3.2` branch:
![Screenshot_20210105_152232](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4701338/103657193-e231b180-4f69-11eb-8e3e-fe22749367ce.png)

Can you still reproduce it, and which Blender version do you use?

Please read the OP carefully, I'm not talking about the GLTF dependencies, this issue concerns the textures that are copied over, they do not get linked to the materials, instead they get packed inside of them, leaving the ones in the texture folder unused.

So check the dependencies of the resulting SpatialMaterials.
Thanks, I can confirm that. The `.material` files are indeed 3 MB of embedded data.

Indeed this change is wrong: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/42504/files#diff-391b8dac176705a7434fd9ca93ac540183658308fcb6a91cc40f6f2ecd4439baR1322-R1338

This causes loading the external images as a byte array instead of a resource if it has a proper `mimeType`, which is wrong.  I'll fix it.

review_comments:
For the reference, aside from changing the order of the conditions, another logic change here is that invalid textures will no longer be added to `state->images`, instead it will throw an error (see `else`).

If preferred, we could still pass an empty `Ref<Texture2D>` to fill the spot instead of errorring out, but I'm not sure if there's any situation where either method would fail and the glTF file would not be bogus.
Actually I think I'll do that, and only throw a warning to identify the potential bogus situation. It's better than an early exit.
The gltf blender plugin creates an empty texture. Will find the pr in a few moments.
